| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | in-progress | 2026-08-11 — library-core-retarget moved to done — the SECOND landing, merged as library#54 after every check passed: library#51's major-aware fixture writers and two seam commits re-landed by cherry-pick, the new enumeration seam, the atomic flip, and the docs sweep, every commit before and after the flip independently green (task check + task cue:check against GHCR with no local registry, flow tests forced with OPM_FLOW_TEST_FORCE=1 materializing the real catalog). The default resolves core v2.0.0-alpha.4 (alpha.5 still not cut at landing time); web_app consumed catalogs/opm 2.0.0-alpha.2 with D49 versioned imports (blueprints/traits/resources at v1beta1) and opm_platform's subscription named the same tag as its scalar version — transitional invariant 1's pin-tracks-newest-tag obligation is live, ENFORCED by the library's repaired cue:catalog:drift check (previously vacuous: jq key hardcoded to the v0 dep form, stable-only tag filter, unpaginated tag listing; it now checks both the web_app dep pin and the platform #registry scalar against the newest tag on their own major line, stable-first with a prerelease fallback mirroring the kernel's highestStable), and bumps with every catalog release until library-acquire-and-subscription makes the pin load-bearing. TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE REDO'S OWN PLAN, both discovered during apply. First, the fourth seam adaptation required NO new resolution logic: cuelang.org/go's modregistry.ModuleVersions already scopes a major-suffixed path to its major (client.go filters tags on semver.Major when ast.SplitPackageVersion finds a suffix), so materialize's existing pass-through of the raw subscription key IS the scoping — what landed is the locking unit test (mixed-major published list modelled on the real repo: a v2-suffixed key selects the highest v2 alpha via the prerelease-only fallback and never stable 0.6.0, a major-free key keeps selecting 0.6.0) plus the enumerate.go doc rewrite. The platform-materialization spec delta's scenarios hold verbatim; only the imagined diff was wrong. Second, web_app initially had to author updateStrategy.rollingUpdate EXPLICITLY although #UpdateStrategySchema marks the field optional, because catalog_opm's deployment-transformer dereferenced #component.spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate unguarded whenever type was RollingUpdate — a component exercising its schema-legal right to omit it failed transform execution with '2 errors in empty disjunction'. RESOLVED THE SAME DAY, catalog-side, not papered over: catalog_opm#37 guards the dereference in the deployment and statefulset transformers AND re-lands the alpha.8 guard-hoisting fix the daemonset transformer never received (its updateStrategy was still silently dropped from every DaemonSet — found while fixing the sibling), all four regression tests proven to fail against the pre-fix code; released as catalogs/opm 2.0.0-alpha.3, verified against the published bytes with an alpha.2 negative control before merging. library#55 then dropped the fixture accommodation — web_app renders the schema-legal omission end-to-end through the flow tests — and moved both pins to 2.0.0-alpha.3, the drift check's first real enforcement. ONE PRE-EXISTING DEVIATION RECONFIRMED: the deep blueprints/workload import at instance_integration_test.go stays pinned to catalog v0.6.0 where that path is correct — D49 does not reopen it, the site pins below both filings. | Module and Catalog Identity |

| [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

| [0015](./0015/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-08-05 — Drafted from a design conversation grounded in three measurements taken the same day. `core/src/catalog.cue` carries exactly ONE member map, `#transformers`, and `library/opm/materialize/index.go:39-41` skips any catalog build without one — so a contract with no adapter is absent from the materialized world, which is precisely the state 0010 D37's `fulfilment: "provider"` creates on purpose. `compile/match.go:344-360` is SUBSET containment, not equality, so a more-specific transformer never displaces a less-specific one; both pair and both render, and 0010 D32's guard does not reach the case because it fires only for `fulfilment: "provider"` contracts. And the real discriminator across the 8 transformers sharing `catalog_opm`'s `#ContainerResource` bucket is `requiredLabels` (`daemonset_transformer.cue:27-29`), not the resource/trait set — which is what makes 0010 D36's `matchLabels` the lever for provider classes rather than a new matcher concept. Four decisions locked: D1 (explicit contract maps), D2 (classes, amending 0010 D37), D3 (RBAC-gated registration CR), D4 (no contract/adapter packaging split, decided now because riding 0010's FQN break is nearly free and a standalone break later is not). Six Open Questions carried. | Catalog Contracts, Provider Classes, and Transformer Registration |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
